English Vowel Sounds

Watch how your mouth makes each sound

Level 3 — Pronunciation

 

Parts of the Mouth

These pictures show the inside of the mouth from the side, like a head cut in half.

 

What Makes a Vowel?

For a vowel, air comes out freely. Nothing stops it. Three things change the sound:

1. Tongue up or down: high · middle · low
2. Tongue forward or back: front · center · back
3. Lips: relaxed or round

Your jaw opens more for the low vowels. Put a finger on your chin and say “see … cat” — feel your jaw drop.

 

The 12 Vowel Sounds

FrontCenterBack
High/i/ see
/ɪ/ sit		/u/ food
/ʊ/ book
Middle/eɪ/ say
/ɛ/ bed		/ə/ about
/ʌ/ cup		/oʊ/ go
Low/æ/ cat/ɔ/ saw
/ɑ/ hot

The back vowels /u ʊ oʊ ɔ/ use round lips. The front vowels use relaxed lips.

 

Front Vowels

The front of the tongue does the work. From high to low:

/i/ see → /ɪ/ sit → /eɪ/ say → /ɛ/ bed → /æ/ cat

Say them in order. Your tongue goes down and your jaw opens a little more each time.

 

/i/ — as in see

Side view — the head turns slowly

Front view

Tongue: high and front  |  Lips: relaxed, a little spread (smile)
Words: see · key · sleep · eat · tree
Try it: Smile a little. Push the front of your tongue up, close to the roof of your mouth.
 

/ɪ/ — as in sit

Side view — the head turns slowly

Front view

Tongue: high and front, a little lower than /i/  |  Lips: relaxed
Words: sit · big · milk · give · win
Try it: Start from /i/, then relax your tongue and let it drop a little. The sound is short.
 

/eɪ/ — as in say

Side view and front view — watch the tongue move

Tongue: starts middle-front, then moves up  |  Lips: relaxed
Words: say · day · rain · name · cake
Try it: This is a glide: start near /ɛ/ and move your tongue up toward /ɪ/.
 

/ɛ/ — as in bed

Side view — the head turns slowly

Front view

Tongue: middle and front  |  Lips: relaxed
Words: bed · red · pen · egg · desk
Try it: Open your mouth a little more than for /eɪ/. Keep your tongue still — no glide.
 

/æ/ — as in cat

Side view — the head turns slowly

Front view

Tongue: low and front  |  Lips: relaxed, jaw open
Words: cat · apple · black · map · sad
Try it: Open your jaw wide. Keep the front of your tongue low and forward.

1. Which word has /i/?

2. Which word has /ɪ/?

Center Vowels

The tongue rests in the middle of the mouth. The lips are relaxed.

/ʌ/ cup — a short sound in a strong (stressed) syllable
/ə/ about — the weak vowel in a syllable with no stress
 

/ʌ/ — as in cup

Side view — the head turns slowly

Front view

Tongue: middle and center  |  Lips: relaxed
Words: cup · bus · love · money · cut
Try it: Short and relaxed. Your tongue rests in the middle of your mouth.
 

/ə/ — as in about

Side view — the head turns slowly

Front view

Tongue: middle and center, very relaxed  |  Lips: relaxed
Words: about · banana · sofa · today
Try it: This is the weak vowel. It only comes in syllables with no stress.
 

Back Vowels

The back of the tongue does the work. From low to high:

/ɑ/ hot → /ɔ/ saw → /oʊ/ go → /ʊ/ book → /u/ food

Say them in order. Your tongue goes up each time, and your lips get rounder toward /u/.

 

/ɑ/ — as in hot

Side view — the head turns slowly

Front view

Tongue: low and back  |  Lips: relaxed, jaw open
Words: hot · stop · job · clock · father
Try it: Open your jaw. Pull your tongue down and back. Say “ah” for the doctor.
 

/ɔ/ — as in saw

Side view — the head turns slowly

Front view

Tongue: low-middle and back  |  Lips: a little round
Words: saw · law · talk · thought
Try it: Round your lips a little. Many people in California say these words with /ɑ/ — both are OK.
 

/oʊ/ — as in go

Side view and front view — watch the tongue move

Tongue: starts middle-back, then moves up  |  Lips: round, then rounder
Words: go · no · home · phone · road
Try it: This is a glide: start with round lips and your tongue in the middle-back, then finish at /ʊ/.
 

/ʊ/ — as in book

Side view — the head turns slowly

Front view

Tongue: high and back, a little lower than /u/  |  Lips: a little round
Words: book · foot · put · cook · wood
Try it: Relax your lips and tongue a little from /u/. The sound is short.
 

/u/ — as in food

Side view — the head turns slowly

Front view

Tongue: high and back  |  Lips: round and pushed forward
Words: food · blue · moon · school · two
Try it: Round your lips into a small circle. Pull the back of your tongue up.

More Glides: /aɪ/ /aʊ/ /ɔɪ/

A glide starts at one vowel and moves to another. Watch the tongue and lips move.

/aɪ/ — as in my

Starts low and center, moves up to /ɪ/: my · night · buy · five

/aʊ/ — as in now

Starts low and center, moves up to /ʊ/ with round lips: now · out · down · loud

/ɔɪ/ — as in boy

Starts at /ɔ/ with round lips, moves up and forward to /ɪ/: boy · toy · oil · enjoy

Exercise 4 — Which Glide?

Say the word slowly. Which glide do you hear: /eɪ/, /oʊ/, /aɪ/, /aʊ/, or /ɔɪ/?

1. time

/aɪ/ — the tongue starts low and moves up to /ɪ/.

2. house

/aʊ/ — the tongue starts low and moves up to /ʊ/, and the lips get round.

3. coin

/ɔɪ/ — the lips start round, then the tongue moves forward to /ɪ/.

4. train

/eɪ/ — the tongue starts middle-front and moves up to /ɪ/.

5. snow

/oʊ/ — the lips are round, and the tongue moves up at the back.

 

Mixed Practice — Word Pairs

Say both words. Feel your tongue, jaw, and lips. Then answer.

1. ship — sheep: Which word has /i/?

sheep — /i/ is higher and longer; ship has /ɪ/.

2. bed — bad: Which word opens your jaw more?

bad — /æ/ is low, so the jaw opens wide; bed has /ɛ/.

3. cup — cop: Which word has the tongue further back?

cop — cop has /ɑ/, low and back; cup has /ʌ/ in the center.

4. pull — pool: Which word has rounder lips?

pool — pool has /u/ with small round lips; pull has /ʊ/, more relaxed.

5. hat — hot: Which word has the tongue further forward?

hat — hat has /æ/, a front vowel; hot has /ɑ/, a back vowel.

6. wait — wet: Which word has a glide?

wait — wait has /eɪ/, which moves; wet has /ɛ/, which stays still.
